 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Daniel.S.Kumar, who met with road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief are that : On 10.03.2023 at about 2.45 to 2.50 p.m., while Daniel.S. Kumar (herein after referred to as the deceased) was proceeding in Apache motor bike bearing reg.No.KA- 01-HU-1196 as a pillion rider and same was ridden by its rider by name Mr.Hari Prasad and when they reached opposite Namadhev Steel Centre, near SBI Bank, Hosur Service Road, Singasandra Bangalore, at that time the driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA-05-MP- 4900 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner from Hosur Main Road, Kiya show room service road towards Kudlu gate and while taking right turn dashed against the deceased motorcycle, result of which the deceased fell down along with motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
the deceased was shifted to Kaveri hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then the deceased was shifted to Campbell Hospital, H.S.R. Layout, wherein taken treatment as an inpatient for one week.
During the course of treatment, he succumbed to the fatal injuries on 15-02-2023.

So far the petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies expenses and Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and also spent an amount of Rs.6, 50,000/-
towards treatment and other medical expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the deceased was very hale and healthy.
The deceased was aged about 25 years.
The deceased was working as a Dominos Pizza Store Manager, Bangalore and was drawing a salary of Rs.18, 000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of deceased, petitioners have suffered pain and mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. The respondent No.1- the insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-05-MP-4900 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of policy subject to its terms and conditions.
They have contended that the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

It is further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01- HU-1196 in which the deceased was travelling, who was riding his motorcycle without driving licence and without wearing helmet as on the date of accident.

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?

Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No 2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

sentences.text: 12. On the basis of the complaint lodged by H.Keshava Murthy, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.0086/2023 of Electronic City Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337, 338 of IPC.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 338, 304(A) of of IPC.
13.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has much argued that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle and that at the time of accident deceased was not wearing helmet and that deceased himself without having valid driving license was riding the motorcycle hence he too has contributed negligence to cause the accident.
14.

In the light of the arguments canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 if the materials placed on record are perused, it is without much delay the complaint was lodged wherein it was clearly stated that the deceased was traveling in the motorcycle as pillion rider.
Further none of the documents disclose that deceased was travelling in the two wheeler as rider.

Admittedly though the respondent no.2 has taken steps to examine the driver of the offending vehicle but they have failed to secure his presence and thereby failed to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, there are no materials placed on record to say that at the time of accident the deceased was riding the motorcycle.

15. So far as not holding valid driving license and not wearing helmet is concerned, it is true that in the seizure mahazar there is no mention about seizure of helmet but none of the police document discloses that at the time of accident the rider and pillion rider were not wearing helmet and rider was not holding valid driving license.

Even if it is taken for a while for the sake of discussion that at the time of accident rider and pillion rider were not wearing helmet and that rider was not holding driving license, then also negligence cannot be attributed against the rider of the motorcycle simply on the ground that they were not wearing helmet and not holding driving license unless the negligence contributed by the rider is proved.

Further if really the rider was not holding valid driving license and they were not wearing helmet then for the violation of Motor Vehicle rules penal provision would attract but it would not be a ground to attribute contributory negligence against the rider of motor cycle.

16. Coming to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the motorcycle was proceeding in service road towards Kodlu gate and the offending vehicle which came from the same direction when it reached the spot of accident has taken right turn towards SBI road.
The accident in question has occurred somewhere in the left side of the said road.

When the driver of the offending vehicle was taking right turn, he has to take all kind of precautionary measures and after confirming that no vehicles are coming on either side near by the place of his taking right turn then only he has to proceed to take turn of the vehicle by giving proper indication.
When motorcycle was proceeding on the straight road and that to at the Kumar.S vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165665353/

When offending vehicle was taking right turn, the right portion of the said vehicle touched on the front portion of the motorcycle result of which the right rear side of the offending vehicle and front side of the motorcycle was damaged.
Hence, the police records coupled with the evidence of PW.1 clearly indicates that the driver of offending vehicle alone has contributed negligence.
Hence rightly after investigation the investigation officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:-

It is the contention that petitioners being the parents of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was working as a Guest Delight Manager at Jubilant Food works Domino's Pizza and drawing salary of Rs.18,000/- p.m.
18.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 25 years.
In this regard, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.12/Aadhaar card of the deceased which show his date of birth as 23-03-1998 and as the accident took place in the year 2023.
Therefore, the deceased was aged about 25 years as on the date of accident.
19. As observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioners that deceased was working as a Guest Delight Manager at Jubilant Food works Domino's Pizza and drawing salary of Rs.18,000/- p.m.

To prove the education and employment of the deceased the petitioners have produced ID card issued by Chai Point company dated 05-12-2019, appointment letter issued by Coldman warehousing and distribution , relieving letter with breakup salary issued by Secure Info, pay slips for the month of December 2022 to March 2023 issued by Jubliant Food works, Jubliant Food works full and final settlement details and Bank statement from 01-07-2023 to 06-04-2023, Migration certificate, SSLC marks card, Diploma in Mechanical, Diploma in Mechanical Engineering as per Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.19 and Ex.P23 to Ex.P26.
20.
If Ex.P14 to Ex.P18 is perused, during the year 2019 the deceased was working in Chai Point Company and drawing salary of Rs.16,822/-.
During the year 2018 he was working as Office Assistant in Coldman Warehousing and Distribution and drawing monthly salary of Rs.18,175/-.

Ex.P16 discloses that he was working as Facility Executive in Secure Info and he has given resignation to the said job on 10-08- 2018 in the said company where in he was drawing salary of Rs.21,012/-.
At the time of accident he was working in Jubliant Food works Limited and he was drawing salary of Rs.15,286/- and there is variation in the salary of the deceased from month to month.
Hence, considering the salary slip produced by the petitioners and there is variation in the monthly salary , this court inclines to take the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/-.

21. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as he was bachelor 50% of annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 50% is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

22. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors/Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held Kumar.S vs Liberty General Insurance Co. 5 that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

sentences.text:
It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation. Hence in the instant case as the victim was 25 years the addition towards future prospect should be 40%
23.
Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/-on which 40% is added towards the future prospect which comes to Rs.21,700/-.
Out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.10,850/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is 18 for the age of the deceased.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.23,43,600/- (10,850/-x 12 x 18).
24. Because of the untimely death of deceased, the petitioner's no1 and 2 have lost their son thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium,
and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

25. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-
26.

In so far as the medical expenses is concerned, the PW.1 has contended that they have spent Rs.4,50,000/- towards treatment of the deceased Daniel S Kumar who was treated at Campbell Hospital, HSR Layout till 15-03-2023.

The petitioners have produced medical bills for a sum of Rs.1,
00,428/-, medical prescriptions, cash receipts as per Ex.P.20 to 22.
There is no contra evidence to discard the medical bills produced by the petitioners.

Therefore,
Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.1,00,428/- under head medical expenses .

28. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.4: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 to 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,77,128/- + cost of Rs.1000/- imposed vide order date 29-04- 2024.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.25,78,128/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh Seventy Eight Thousand One Hundred Twenty Eight only).
A sum of Rs.25,77,128/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the amount along with interest within two months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner no1 is entitled for Rs.9,78128/- Petitioner no 2 is entitled for Rs.16,00,000/-

Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 2 shall be deposited in their names in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner no.1 and 2 on proper identification.
